entwurf.thema: Cleaning Ads & Bloatware from an Old Android TV with Claude Code
entwurf.beschreibung: An old Android TV is clogged with ad‑laden apps and hidden bloatware. Using Claude Code’s script‑writing AI you can strip the junk, speed up launches and regain a quiet living‑room. The guide walks you through each step, shows the real limits, and peppers the process with jokes that keep the frustration light.

teile.name: Hook
teile.szene: A modern living room, night light, TV glowing with banner ads
teile.text: Your TV streams ads like a popcorn machine at a rave—loud, nonstop, and eating bandwidth.

teile.name: Problem
teile.szene: Living room, people frustrated, ads popping while movie plays
teile.text: Those ads hog bandwidth, slow apps, and ruin movie night. It feels like watching a film while someone keeps blowing up the popcorn machine in the background.

teile.name: Tool Intro
teile.szene: Workspace, laptop open, Claude Code interface
teile.text: Enter Claude Code, the AI that writes scripts while you sip coffee. It’s like hiring a genius intern who forgets everything at midnight—the code does the work, then disappears.

teile.name: Step 1 – Install Claude Code
teile.szene: Laptop screen, terminal open, command line showing curl
teile.text: Install Claude Code on your laptop: `curl -sSL https://install.claude.com | sh`. It’s as simple as ordering pizza, but you get to choose the toppings yourself.

teile.name: CTA 1
teile.szene: Screen with share icon, user looking at it
teile.text: If this helps, like, share, and save for later!

teile.name: Step 2 – Generate Uninstall Script
teile.szene: Claude Code interface generating bash code
teile.text: Ask Claude Code: “Write a bash script to list all installed packages on Android TV and remove any that contain ‘ad’.” The assistant writes the code, and you feel like you just hired a robot butler.

teile.name: Result 1 – Script Output
teile.szene: Terminal showing script with adb commands
teile.text: Claude outputs a one‑liner: `adb shell pm list packages | grep ad | while read p; do adb shell pm uninstall $p; done`. It’s efficient, but also a bit like a ghost that cleans up after you.

teile.name: Step 3 – Connect ADB
teile.szene: Laptop connected to TV via USB‑ADB, TV screen shows connect prompt
teile.text: Connect your laptop to the TV via ADB: `adb connect <TV_IP>`. Think of it as plugging the TV into your brain’s Wi‑Fi router.

teile.name: Step 4 – Run the Script
teile.szene: Terminal executing script, TV screen clearing ads
teile.text: Run the script. Watch the TV purge ad apps like a magician pulling rabbits out of a hat. The screen is suddenly empty, like a clean canvas ready for the next masterpiece.

teile.name: Joke 1
teile.text: It’s like hiring a genius intern who forgets everything at midnight—the script does the work, then disappears.

teile.name: Limitation 1 – Developer Mode
teile.szene: TV settings showing locked developer mode option
teile.text: ADB needs developer mode on the TV; some manufacturers lock it down. It’s like trying to open a locked box with a rubber hammer.

teile.name: Joke 2
teile.text: Trying to uninstall ads on a TV that refuses updates is like polishing a statue that’s already marble. You get dust, but the shape stays the same.

teile.name: Step 5 – Verify Speed
teile.szene: TV launching app faster after cleanup
teile.text: Reboot the TV and run a benchmark app; you should see faster launch times. The difference is subtle, like a sprinter in a marathon.

teile.name: Joke 3
teile.text: Now the TV loads apps as quickly as a snail on a treadmill – slower, but at least it’s moving. It’s better than standing still, right?

teile.name: Limitation 2 – Token Overhead
teile.text: Claude Code adds about 33 k tokens before your prompt, increasing API cost – not free if you run many TVs. Think of it as a bill that arrives after the party.

teile.name: Safety Tip
teile.text: Back up your TV’s data first; a rogue script can uninstall system apps. It’s the same as backing up your life before jumping off a cliff.

teile.name: Payoff
teile.szene: TV screen showing movie, no ads, people relaxing
teile.text: After cleanup, your TV streams movies without interruption – the popcorn stays in the bowl. You finally get to enjoy the show without a pop‑up spoiler.
